Disrepute

/dis-ri-PYOOT/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Disrepute means a state of being held in low regard or having a bad reputation.

Disrepute means a state of being held in low regard or having a bad reputation. Years of falsified data brought the once-celebrated research laboratory into disrepute, and other scientists quietly stopped citing its studies.

Worked Example

Sunny Terrace, once the most popular restaurant on the boardwalk, fell into disrepute after inspectors published a string of serious kitchen violations. Within a month, its dining room sat nearly empty even on summer weekends.

The restaurant's damaged reputation, and the public's loss of trust in it, shows exactly what it means to fall into disrepute.

How Disrepute Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disgrace

disgrace: loss of respect or honor

dishonor

dishonor: a state of shame or lost respect

shame

shame: a painful loss of standing or respect

Antonyms

esteem

esteem: high respect and admiration

prestige

prestige: widespread respect based on reputation

How Strong Is It? — unpopularity → disrepute → infamy

unpopularity vs. disrepute

unpopularity vs. disrepute: Unpopularity just means people do not like something at the moment, while disrepute means its reputation itself has been seriously damaged.

infamy vs. disrepute

infamy vs. disrepute: Disrepute means being held in low regard, but infamy means being widely famous for something truly shameful.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: not, opposite of

Root — repute

Root — repute: from Latin reputare, to think well of

Put it together

Put it together: Disrepute is a textbook case of dis- meaning 'not, opposite of': dis- plus repute, from Latin reputare, 'to think well of.' To be in disrepute is literally to be 'not well thought of.'

Use the root in a new word: reputable

Use the root in a new word: reputable: Choose a reputable repair shop that stands behind its work, since reputable literally describes a business that people think well of.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Disrepute almost always appears in the fixed phrases 'fall into disrepute' and 'bring something into disrepute.' It names the lasting state of a damaged reputation, not a single embarrassing moment.
